Definition: apparently from σκέλλω (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank):--leg.
BiblicalUsage: Skelos is the leg, and all three occurrences are at the cross. The Jews asked Pilate that the legs of the crucified might be broken so the bodies would not remain on the Sabbath, the soldiers brake the legs of the two thieves, and when they came to Jesus they saw He was dead already, and brake not His legs.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the unbroken legs are the proof that Scripture is kept to the letter, because not a bone of Him was broken.
